criteria.description: Includes a mock launch-day press release written from the customer's point of view, leading with the customer problem and benefit (not the company/tech), with a believable customer quote.
The press release uses plain, specific language a normal person would find compelling — not jargon/buzzword filler.
Includes an FAQ that tackles the hard questions — why customers will care, why us, biggest risks, what we're NOT doing, and/or how it makes money — rather than only easy ones.
Quantifies or makes concrete the customer benefit (e.g. time saved vs. today) rather than vague 'saves time'.
Ends with an honest judgment on whether the idea is compelling/worth building (build / reshape / drop), including what's weak or risky.
